PUBLIC RESPONSE: From a bird’s-eye view the two campuses are the classic Pisa Piagge
complex. The Galilei-Pacinotti block and the Ulisse Dini block sit side-by-side on
the same lot with the inter-block court opening to the south. The two rectangular
masses with the court between them give the whole site the squared-U / C
outline that in the local description is read as the capital U – the familiar
H-shaped / G-shaped school court that is normally talked about as a big U,
sometimes rendered as a C/G in the popular aerial photos. That is the “letter’’
that the two adjoining institutes make on the map.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: From a satellite / aerial view the two contiguous complexes in
Via della Foce / Via delle Cascine are not two independent blocks but one
continuous perimeter. The Galilei-Pacinotti block on the west and the
Ulisse Dini block on the east close on each other on the north and south
and leave an open court to the south. In plan that is the classic Italian
scuola-a-cortile perimeter, i.e. a big capital C / U. In the local
description of the site the silhouette is habitually quoted as the
capital P / U that is made by the two institutes standing shoulder to
shoulder, the open side of the C being the street front. That is the
U / C shape that is normally illustrated as a P from above.

2.text:

plan. The ITIS Galileo Galilei – E. Pacinotti block and the Liceo
Scientifico Ulisse Dini block are built as two long parallel wings
joined by the intermediate low-rise / service block on Viale delle
Piagge. In the usual schematic description the plan is the capital
that is quoted locally as an A–/ H– shaped school campus, the two
wings being the legs of the A and the connecting block the cross-bar,
the configuration that in ordinary parlance is rendered as the H/U
shaped “A” of the Galilei-Pacinotti / Dini complex. That is the
aerial letter that is normally shown for the two neighbouring
istituti.

5.text:
The planimetria that you see on a satellite / ortho-photo of the
Viale/Piazza di San Zeno / Via Galilei area is the classic post-war
Italian school block.

The I.T.I.S. “Galilei–Pacinotti” is the big rectangular stem with its
central cortile and the Liceo Classico / Scientifico “Ulisse Dini” is the
rectangular block set immediately alongside it on the west side, linked
by the transversal passage that closes the two courtyards.  Put together
the two adjacent blocks give the familiar double-bar plan that is
normally read from the air as an H-plan, i.e. the P-shaped school
complex that the two istituti form together in the neighbourhood of
Porta a Mare.  That is the H / P-shaped silhouette that is usually quoted
for the Galilei-Pacinotti / Dini pair.
